why: In an unweighted tree, distances from a fixed vertex come from one BFS. Run BFS three times (from x, y and z) to get every vertex's three distances, then test each vertex's sorted triple for a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
hints: You need dist(v, x), dist(v, y), dist(v, z) for every v. What computes all distances from one source in an unweighted graph?
Three BFS runs, one from each fixed vertex, each O(n).
For each vertex, sort its three distances, skip it if the smallest is 0, and check a*a + b*b == c*c. O(n) overall.
pitfalls: A vertex at distance 0 from any of x, y, z never counts.
x, y, z may coincide; three BFS runs still work.
